note: Trigger function that copies customer_id into customer_id_new on every insert (and on any update of customer_id).

Add a nullable bigint column customer_id_new (metadata only, no table rewrite) and the sync trigger in one transaction, so every row inserted from now on has it filled. Short lock_timeout with retries, so the app's queries never queue behind this for long.
Backfill customer_id_new for ids 1..1000000, 100000 rows per statement (row locks on existing rows only; the app never updates orders).
Backfill the rest: orders the app inserted before the trigger existed (ids above 10000000). Later inserts are filled by the trigger.
Add CHECK (customer_id_new IS NOT NULL) NOT VALID: a brief lock and no scan; enforced for new rows from now on. Retries on a short lock_timeout.
Validate the check: a full scan under SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE, which does not block the app's reads or inserts. Fails, and stops the plan, if any row was missed.
Verify every row has customer_id_new = customer_id before the swap; raises, and stops the plan, on any mismatch.

Swap in one short transaction: SET NOT NULL (no scan; the validated check proves it), drop the trigger, drop the old integer column, rename customer_id_new to customer_id, drop the now-redundant check. All metadata only, so the exclusive lock is held for milliseconds. The app keeps using the name customer_id, so no deploy is needed. Retries on a short lock_timeout.
Drop the sync trigger function, no longer used.
Check the result: orders.customer_id is bigint NOT NULL; raises otherwise.
Reclaim the dead row versions left by the backfill and refresh statistics (does not block reads or writes).
